- Legacy `anon` JWT `eyJ...`

Our code accepts either — it just passes it as `apikey` header and to createClient. supabase-js v2.116 supports publishable keys. Note: for auth flows, anon JWT also used as fallback... createClient works.

Wait — one important check: our code sends `apikey` header and uses `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`. With publishable keys, supabase-js handles it; the raw fetch to Edge Functions with `apikey: sb_publishable_...` is valid (Edge Function gateway accepts publishable key in apikey header). Yes, Supabase docs say publishable keys work via `apikey` header for functions. Good.

Also: RLS policies in schema.sql match roles `anon`/`authenticated` — publishable key maps to anon role, so fine.

Also mention: their project may not yet have publishable keys created (older projects); then Settings > API Keys has tabs "Publishable and secret API keys" and legacy.

The key lives in the Supabase dashboard for your project (`junygonfegrwwwvnxhoa`). There are two interchangeable names for it now — Supabase is retiring the old ones during 2026:

- **Publishable key** — `sb_publishable_…` (the current name, recommended)
- **Legacy anon key** — a long `eyJ…` JWT (still works, but deprecated at the end of 2026)

Either one works with this app; it just passes the value as the `apikey` header and to `createClient()`. Keep the *variable* named `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` regardless of which format you copy, because that's the exact name the code reads at [supabase-client.js:19](js/supabase-client.js#L19).

    const m = raw.match(/^\s*([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s*=\s*(.*)$/);
    if (!m || m[1] !== name) continue;
    let v = m[2].trim();
    if ((v.startsWith('"') && v.endsWith('"')) || (v.startsWith("'") && v.endsWith("'"))) {
      v = v.slice(1, -1);
    }
    return v.replace(/\\n/g, "").trim();
  }
  return "";
}

const url = readVar("SUPABASE_DB_URL");

  console.error("SUPABASE_DB_URL not found in .env");
  process.exit(2);
}

  ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },

});

  const seedSql = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, "supabase/seed-tests.sql"), "utf8");

  console.log("applied supabase/seed-tests.sql");

  const tables = await client.query(`
    select table_name from information_schema.tables
    where table_schema = 'public' order by table_name`);
  const counts = {};
  for (const { table_name } of tables.rows) {
    const c = await client.query(`select count(*)::int as n from public."${table_name}"`);
    counts[table_name] = c.rows[0].n;
  }
  const policies = await client.query(`
    select tablename, policyname, cmd, roles::text as roles
    from pg_policies where schemaname = 'public' order by tablename, policyname`);
  const fns = await client.query(`
    select p.proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid) as args

  const views = await client.query(`
    select table_name from information_schema.views

  console.log("functions:", fns.rows.map((r) => `${r.proname}(${r.args})`).join(", ") || "(none)");
  console.log("rls:", JSON.stringify(rls.rows));
  console.log("policies:", JSON.stringify(policies.rows, null, 2));
  summary.push("ok");
} catch (err) {

  }
  process.exitCode = 1;
} finally {
  await client.end().catch(() => {});
}

# Kredora — Developer Proof Platform

> **Don't just claim a skill. Prove it.** Solve coding problems with server-side grading, build a timestamped, tamper-evident evidence ledger, and share a profile backed by real execution data.

Kredora is a multi-page static web app for practicing coding problems and accumulating verifiable evidence of skill: every accepted submission is graded in a sandbox, stored on Supabase, and chained into a tamper-evident ledger.

---

## Architecture

Kredora is a **multi-page static site** — no client-side router and no Node server in production. Vite bundles the JS, Tailwind (v4, via the Vite plugin) compiles the CSS, and the output is deployed as plain static files.

**Pages** (each a separate Vite build input):

| Page | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Landing page (marketing demos are labeled as examples) |
| `login.html` / `signup.html` | Supabase Auth (email + password) |
| `dashboard.html` | Real stats, skill rings, recent activity, achievements |
| `problem-list.html` | Coding problem catalog with filters |
| `problem.html` | In-browser editor + submission flow |
| `evidence.html` | Evidence ledger: verified submissions + user-added projects/assessments |
| `profile.html` | Shareable profile computed from your own data |
| `skill.html` | Per-skill breakdown |
| `privacy.html` / `terms.html` | Template policy pages (marked for legal review) |

**Key JS modules** (`js/`):

- `user-stats.js` — the single source for all user numbers (solved counts, streak from consecutive submission days, verified points by difficulty, per-skill progress). Every page reads the same functions, so the numbers always agree.
- `skills.js` — config declaring the tracked skills (Java, JavaScript, SQL, MongoDB) and which evidence types feed each.
- `problems-data.js` — the problem catalog and local progress tracker. Hidden test cases are stripped from the client bundle at load; only sample tests ship to the browser.
- `supabase-client.js` — Supabase singleton, submission calls, verify-record client.
- `site-config.js` — the one place the site URL, tagline, and identity strings are defined.
- `auth.js` — sign-up / sign-in / session handling, with a localStorage fallback when Supabase isn't configured.

---

## Supabase setup

Kredora uses Supabase for auth, database, and Edge Functions. To wire up your own project:

1. Create a project at [supabase.com](https://supabase.com).
2. Run the full schema: [`supabase/schema.sql`](supabase/schema.sql) — tables (`problem_submissions`, `user_progress`, `problem_tests`, `submission_rate_limits`, `submission_rate_limit_config`, `problems`), the atomic `consume_rate_limit` rate-limiting function, the `profile_summaries` view, and Row Level Security policies. Clients get owner-SELECT only; **inserts into `problem_submissions` happen exclusively via the Edge Function using the service-role key** — there are no client INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies. The `problems` table is the authoritative problem record (existence, difficulty, points) validated server-side on every submission; the client problem list is display-only. Rate limiting is enforced server-side by the Edge Function (fail-closed, atomic, DB-clock based) and is tunable via the `submission_rate_limit_config` table or `RATE_LIMIT_*` Edge Function secrets.
3. Seed the server-side hidden tests: [`supabase/seed-tests.sql`](supabase/seed-tests.sql) (generated by `scripts/generate-seed-tests.mjs`). `problem_tests` has RLS enabled and forced with **zero policies**, so hidden tests are unreadable from the browser.

**Root cause:** GitHub Pages was serving your raw source files, not the compiled build. In raw source, three layers break at once:

**[run-submission/index.ts](supabase/functions/run-submission/index.ts) (edge function)**

- **Response payload removed of all per-test detail.** `testResults: outcomes` is gone. The submission response is now only: `ok, status (overall verdict), allPassed, passedCount, totalCount, runtime, memory, recordId, recordHash`, plus `compileError` (added only when a compile error occurred — `JSON.stringify` drops it when `undefined`).

This matters because the JavaScript harness embeds the hidden input into the generated source (`const __args = [...]`), and JS/Judge0 quote the offending source line in syntax errors — filtering those lines prevents the hidden input leaking via a syntax-error snippet.
- **Hash chain untouched**: `testsSummary` (per-test pass bitmask), `codeHash`, predecessor lookup and the two-phase stamp logic are byte-for-byte unchanged — the interesting detail is that the per-test bitmask still exists and is hashed, it just never reaches the client now.
